walkthroughs.body_html: Loftus & Palmer (1974) Exp 1: 45 students watched a car crash clip. Mean speed estimates: smashed 40.8mph, collided 39.3, bumped 38.1, hit 34.0, contacted 31.8. Exp 2: a week later, 32% of 'smashed' group falsely recalled broken glass vs 14% of 'hit' group.

Gabbert et al. (2003) paired participants who saw different videos of the same crime. 71% of those who discussed it reported details they hadn't seen — vs 0% of controls. Memory conformity blurs witnessed and discussed information.

Loftus argued the false glass result was substitution bias — memory itself was altered. Others argue response bias — only the answer changes, not the memory. The brain may reconsolidate memory each time it's accessed.
